resources.string: Wallet (Home Screen)

The main screen you see when the app opens. If you have not added a card, you see a welcome image and the \"Add ID Card\" button. With a card saved, you see your card and the \"Verify with QR code\" button.

Without a card:
1. Start adding a card with "Add ID Card".
2. The "How It Works?" link under the button opens this guide.
3. The gear icon at the top right opens Settings.

With a card saved:
1. "Verify with QR code" opens the QR scanner.
2. The "Remove Identity" link at the bottom removes the card from this phone. You can also delete the card's transaction history, and back it up first.

• Card not showing: VerifyBlind has no accounts; your card lives only on this phone. If you deleted and reinstalled the app, add your card again.\n• fingerprint, face unlock or screen lock asked at every launch: \"Biometric Lock\" is on in Settings; you can turn it off.\n• Connecting takes long or fails after \"Verify with QR code\": check your internet connection and try again.

Your identity ticket stays only on this phone, encrypted. The key that opens it is kept in Android Keystore (in hardware-protected storage on phones that support it) and can be used only with your fingerprint, face unlock or screen lock approval. Our servers keep no copy of your identity data.
Adding a Card (4 Steps)
The flow where you add your ID card to the app. The bar at the top shows the steps: Prepare → MRZ → NFC → Face.

1. Prepare: read the tips, look at the "Read Privacy Notice" link, tick the consent box and tap "Start".
2. MRZ: hold the back of your ID card to the camera. The three-line text area at the bottom is read automatically.
3. NFC: tap the card to the phone and hold it still until reading finishes.
4. Face: approve the biometric data consent. After a short preparation screen, tap "Start" and make the five moves you are asked for.
5. The data goes encrypted to the verification server. If the checks pass, the success screen opens.

• If NFC is off, the app sends you to the NFC setting; turn it on and come back.
• If the card cannot be read, the app retries three times silently; if it still fails, an error message appears. Remove the case and try again.
• Only the new Turkish ID card with an NFC chip is accepted. Passports, the old identity booklet and driving licences are not accepted.
• Users under 15 cannot add a card.
• An expired card cannot be added.

Card data and face frames are encrypted on the phone and opened only inside an isolated environment called AWS Nitro Enclave. There the card\'s government signature, the chip\'s authenticity, liveness and the face match are checked. Then an encrypted ticket that only your phone can open is created. Your identity data is not stored on the server.
NFC Reading
The step that reads the government-signed data on your ID card\'s chip.

1. When "Touch the chip of your identity card to the back of your phone" appears, bring the card to the back of the phone.
2. The NFC reader is usually at the top or middle of the back; slide the card slowly until it connects.
3. When "Reading..." and the progress bar appear, keep the phone and card still (about 10 seconds).
4. When reading finishes, the face step starts.

• If NFC is off, the app sends you to the NFC setting; turn it on and come back.
• Metal or carbon cases block reading; remove the phone and card cases.
• If reading stops halfway, the app retries three times silently. If it still fails, an error message appears; move the card away and bring it back.
• Keep other cards and metal objects away from between the card and the phone.
• Only the new Turkish ID card with an NFC chip is accepted; passports and the old identity booklet do not work.

Data read from the chip is checked inside the enclave against the government signing certificates and revocation lists for ID cards. The chip also signs a code unique to this operation with its own key, so a copied chip cannot pass.
Face and Liveness
The step that shows the person adding the card is its owner and a real, live person. Adding a card asks for five short moves.

1. Follow the tips on the "Before you start" screen: light from the front, phone at eye level, glasses or hat off. Then tap "Start".
2. Bring your face into the frame. If needed, the app asks you to move the phone closer or farther.
3. Make the move shown on screen: blink, smile, open your mouth or blink twice. How to do it is written under the move.
4. Before each move, relax your face and wait for the prompt. After five moves, adding the card continues on its own.

• If you cannot bring your face into the frame within 20 seconds, or do not make a move within 12 seconds, time runs out; start again with "Try Again".
• If you make 3 wrong moves in one step or 5 in total, "Too Many Incorrect Moves" appears.
• If your face leaves the frame during a move, only that step repeats.
• Only one person may be in the frame.
• The screen shows a live similarity score against your chip photo; it must reach at least 65%. Darkness or light from behind lowers it.

The order of the moves comes from the server for each operation and cannot be known in advance. The move frames and the selected face frame go encrypted to the enclave. There it checks that the face in every frame belongs to the same person as the card photo and that the image is not a screen or a photo. The frames are not stored.
Verify with QR
Used when a site or app asks you to prove your identity. You either scan the QR on the site or tap the site\'s verification link in your phone\'s browser; both open the same approval screen.

1. Open the QR scanner with "Verify with QR code" in the Wallet and point the camera at the site's QR.
2. The approval screen shows the site's name and what it asks for (e.g. "Age verification (18+)" or "A permanent recognition code unique to you").
3. Read the privacy notice, tick the consent box and tap "Approve".
4. Approve with fingerprint, face unlock or screen lock.
5. On the "Confirm it is you" screen, look at the camera and make the one move you are asked for.
6. "Success! ✅" appears and the result is sent to the site.

• "Invalid QR": a QR is valid for 15 minutes and can be used once. Refresh the page and scan the new QR.
• If you tap "Reject", the operation is cancelled and nothing is sent to the site.
• If the move is not detected in the face check, the app tries again; after three tries the verification is cancelled. Try again somewhere bright.
• The face check must be done by the person who added the card; if someone else does it, the verification is rejected.
• To undo a verification, swipe the entry right in Settings > Transaction History.

The site does not see your identity. It gets only the answer to its question (e.g. whether you are over 18) and, if it asked, a recognition code for that site only. This code cannot be matched with other sites\' codes.
Transaction History
The list of your card additions, verifications and undo actions. Open it from Settings > Transaction History; opening it asks for fingerprint, face unlock or screen lock.

1. Approve with fingerprint, face unlock or screen lock.
2. Swipe an entry LEFT: it is deleted from the history on this phone.
3. Swipe an entry RIGHT:
 • On a verification: "Revoke Verification" withdraws the consent you gave that site and asks it to delete its records of this verification.
 • On a card addition: "Withdraw Card Registration Consent" withdraws consent and removes the card from the app.
4. The "BACKUP" button above the list opens the backup screen.

• If a connection error appears while undoing, check your internet and try again.\n• Swiping an entry that was already undone does nothing.\n• The history lives only on this phone. Deleting the app deletes it too; back it up first if you want to keep it.
The history is stored encrypted on the phone and is not sent to the server. When you undo a verification, the site is told right away if it has set up a notification address.
Settings
Opened with the gear icon at the top right of the Wallet.

In order:
1. Biometric Lock: when on, the app asks for fingerprint, face unlock or screen lock at every launch. It is off by default.
2. Transaction History.
3. System Security: identity details of the verification server the app connects to.
4. How It Works: this guide.
5. FAQ: frequently asked questions.
6. Contact Us: send feedback or report a problem.
7. Encrypted Backup: back up or restore your transaction history.
8. Language: Turkish, English or the phone's language.
9. Delete My Data: deletes all VerifyBlind data on this phone.
10. Privacy Notice and the terms you accepted.

• Biometric Lock won\'t turn on: your phone needs a fingerprint, face unlock or screen lock. Set one up in the phone\'s security settings first.\n• After \"Delete My Data\" the app returns to first-launch state; you need to add your card again.

\"Delete My Data\" permanently deletes your card, ticket, keys and transaction history from this phone. Backup files you saved to your cloud account are not deleted; you can delete them in your cloud provider.
System Security
Shows the identity of the verification server (AWS Nitro Enclave) the app connects to. Open it from Settings > System Security.

1. The "HARDWARE PROTECTION ACTIVE" heading at the top.
2. Enclave Fingerprint (PCR0): a digest of the code running on the server.
3. Authorized Publisher: VerifyBlind, who signed the code.
4. Verification Status: ✅ Hardware Verified, ⚠️ Developer Mode (Mock) or ❌ Unverified, with the last check time below.
5. "View Source Code" opens the server code on GitHub.
• If you see \"❌ Unverified\", do not verify; update the app or write to us via Settings > Contact Us.\n• \"Not checked yet\" means the connection has not been made yet; check your internet.

PCR0 is the fingerprint of the code on the server. If the app sees a PCR0 that VerifyBlind has not signed, it sends no identity data to that server. The source code is public; anyone can check that the same code gives the same PCR0.
Encrypted Backup
Backs up your transaction history to a single .vfbackup file, or restores it on a new phone. Nothing is uploaded automatically. Your card and ticket are not in the backup.

To back up:
1. Settings > Encrypted Backup > "Back up".
2. Choose where: Google Drive, Dropbox or "Save to file".
3. Keep "Encrypt (recommended)" ticked and enter a password of at least 6 characters.
4. Tap "Back up".

To restore:
1. Tap "Restore" and pick the location and the file.
2. If the file is encrypted, enter its password.
3. Entries are added to your current history; the same entry is never added twice.

"Delete all" deletes all transaction history on this phone.

• If you forget the password, an encrypted backup cannot be opened; keep the password somewhere safe.\n• If the Google Drive or Dropbox sign-in does not open, check your internet and any browser blocker.\n• Moving to a new phone: install VerifyBlind, add your card, then load the backup with \"Restore\".

In an encrypted backup the key is derived from your password; the password never goes to our server or to the cloud provider. If you choose to save without encryption, anyone with access to your cloud account can see which sites you verified with and when.
🛡️ SECURITY & PRIVACY

string-array.name: faq_cat_security_questions
string-array.item: Where is my identity data stored?
Is my national ID number shared with partners?
Is my face photo saved?
Is my data encrypted?
If my phone is stolen, can my data be accessed?

string-array.name: faq_cat_security_answers
string-array.item: Only on your phone. When you add a card and at every verification, the data is encrypted on the phone and opened only inside an isolated environment called AWS Nitro Enclave; it is deleted there after the checks. The ticket on your phone is encrypted and cannot be opened without fingerprint, face unlock or screen lock approval.

No. The site gets only the answer to its question, for example whether you are over 18, as yes or no. Your date of birth is not sent. If the site asks and you approve, it also gets a recognition code for that site only; the code cannot be turned back into your ID number and cannot be matched with other sites\' codes.

Not on our servers. Face frames go encrypted to the enclave, are compared with the card photo there and are not stored. The photo from your card\'s chip stays only inside the encrypted ticket on your phone, so it can be compared at every verification.

Yes. The phone encrypts the data with AES-GCM before sending it; the key is wrapped with RSA-OAEP so that only the enclave can open it. The server in between cannot see the content. The ticket and transaction history on your phone are encrypted too.

Opening your ticket needs the phone\'s fingerprint, face unlock or screen lock approval. Every verification also includes a face check; if the face does not match the person who added the card, the verification is rejected. You can also lock the app at every launch with \"Biometric Lock\" in Settings.

resources.string: 📲 USAGE

string-array.name: faq_cat_usage_questions
string-array.item: Can I undo a verification I already approved?
How do I verify my identity?
How does the partner QR code work?
How does it work on mobile sites without a QR?
Where can I see my transaction history?
How do I back up and move to a new phone?

string-array.name: faq_cat_usage_answers
string-array.item: Yes. In Settings > Transaction History, swipe the verification RIGHT and confirm \"Revoke Verification\". Your consent is withdrawn; if the site has set up a notification address, it is told right away to delete its records.

After adding your card once:
• scan the site's QR with "Verify with QR code" in the Wallet, or
• tap the site's verification link in your phone's browser; the app opens by itself.
On the approval screen you see what the site asks for, approve, confirm with fingerprint, face unlock or screen lock and make one move in a short face check. You do not need to scan your card again.
The QR holds only a one-time operation code that is valid for 15 minutes. The app uses it to fetch the site\'s name and request from the server; nothing is sent until you approve.
If VerifyBlind is installed on your phone, the site\'s verification link opens the app and the approval screen appears directly.
Settings > Transaction History. Card additions, verifications and undo actions are listed there. Opening it asks for fingerprint, face unlock or screen lock.

Use Settings > Encrypted Backup > \"Back up\" to save your transaction history to Google Drive, Dropbox or a file; setting a password is recommended. On the new phone, install VerifyBlind and add your card, then load the backup with \"Restore\". Your card is not in the backup; you add it again on the new phone.

resources.string: 🔧 TROUBLESHOOTING

string-array.name: faq_cat_troubleshooting_questions
string-array.item: My phone does not read the card\'s NFC chip. What should I do?
What should I pay attention to during face verification?
Can I use it without an internet connection?
My card was stolen or lost. What should I do?

string-array.name: faq_cat_troubleshooting_answers
string-array.item:
Try in order:
✓ Make sure NFC is on (if it is off, the app sends you to the setting).
✓ Remove the phone and card cases.
✓ Slide the card slowly over the back of the phone to find the reader (usually the top or middle).
✓ Once "Reading..." appears, keep still until it finishes.

✓ Light should come from the front, with no window or lamp behind you.
✓ Do not wear glasses, a hat or a mask.
✓ Hold the phone steady at eye level.
✓ Before each move, relax your face, wait for the prompt, then make the move.
✓ Adding a card asks for five moves, verifying asks for one. You have 12 seconds for each move.
No. Adding a card and verifying need encrypted communication with the server. Without internet you can see your card and transaction history but cannot verify.

The card alone is not enough to verify; it also takes the phone that added it, that phone\'s lock and the face check at every verification. Someone who finds the card and tries to add it to their own phone will not match the card photo. When you get your new card, add it to the app. If you have questions, write to us via Settings > Contact Us.

resources.string: 📦 SUPPORT & SCOPE

string-array.name: faq_cat_support_questions
string-array.item: Why is face verification needed?
Which documents are supported?
Can I use the app if my phone has no NFC?

string-array.name: faq_cat_support_answers
string-array.item: It proves that the person using the card and phone is the card\'s owner. When you add a card, your face is compared with the chip photo, and at every later verification it is compared with that photo again. So someone who gets hold of your card or phone cannot verify in your name.
Only the new Republic of Türkiye ID card with an NFC chip. Passports, the old identity booklet and driving licences are not accepted. Users under 15 cannot add a card.
No. NFC is needed to read the chip. If your phone has no NFC, the app tells you when you start adding a card.
